newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up, platinum firms on covering.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up, platinum firms on covering.

text.p: Firmer platinum prices helped the precious metals complex hold higher overnight levels on Wednesday but expectations were that they would do no more than trade their narrow ranges, dealers said.
Gold and silver were mildly firmer behind platinum.
Bullion fixed at $369.00 versus $368.20 per ounce previously and a close in London of $368.70/$369.20.
"Things are getting very much into a pre-Christmas vein. It is going to take a big move in the dollar or something to get anything moving," one dealer said.
Most of platinum's momentum came from Tokyo, dealers said.
"It was the last dealing day for the December contract on Tocom and peple were expecting a lot of selling. When that did not happen, they were caught a bit on the hop," a dealer said.
The resultant short-covering in Tokyo took the local spot platinum price into a day's range of $3.25 to close at $372.00/$372.75 from an opening of $368.75/$369.50.
Platinum was indicated at $370.50/$371.50 in London, up $3.65, having fixed at $371.00, its highest since December 6.
"It looks like platinum is in a $369.00-$372.00 range probably until after the holidays," a dealer said.
Gold was forecast to remain between $368.00 and $370.00.
"You've got to trade the range and people seem to be quite content to let it settle between these figures," a dealer said.
A feature of the gold market this week has been the easier tone in forward rates, especially over the year-end, dealers said.

"This could be indicative of some institutional material coming into the market. Some of the banks may have put metal aside for EMU (European Monetary Union) convergence purposes which they can put on offer until it is needed," a dealer said.
Usually the central banks are reluctant to lend gold over the year-end when they perform audits, the dealer added.
"This has surprised people quite a bit. The gold might be earmarked to be sold to another central bank later," he said.

Dealers said the selling by producers which had depressed the market recently had dried up ahead of next week's holiday but the decision in Washington last night not to raise interest rates had not been a significant factor.
Silver's firmer tone on Tuesday, which held overnight, came from fund short-covering, dealers said.
Silver was indicated unchanged at $4.86/$4.88 while palladium was a little easier at $117.50/$118.50 after a close at $118.25/$119.25. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
